newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia gov't calls for review of MinFin freezes.
newsitem.headline: Russia gov't calls for review of MinFin freezes.

text.p: The Russian government called on the judicial authorities to review recent freezes of MinFin bonds, a senior official said on Wednesday.
The official, who asked not to be named, said a meeting chaired by First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin, who is in charge of economic policy, took place on Tuesday.

The meeting was attended by officials from the Finance Ministry, Interior Ministry, Central Bank, Prosecutor-General's office, Vneshekonombank (the paying agent for MinFin bonds) and Vneshtorgbank (the main depositary).
A spokeswoman for Potanin said the meeting also called on the Interior Ministry and Prosecutor-General's office to refrain from any actions which could damage bondholders' rights.

"There was a meeting yesterday where it was recommended to the Prosecutor General and Interior Ministry to refrain from damaging the rights of people who own bonds in good faith," Larisa Zelkova told Reuters.
Zelkova said the meeting also called for the judicial authorities to draw up proposals within 10 days to remove discrepancies in Russia's criminal and civil codes affecting the bonds.
Under criminal law police may freeze bonds which are said to be stolen, but under civil law bonds may not be seized from owners who acquired them in good faith.
The government would then submit the proposals to parliament as an amendment to existing legislation.

A Moscow district prosecutor's office issued an order to freeze $56.81 million face value in June. The bonds were frozen as part of an investigation into the head of a small bank which has since closed.

This would bring the total bonds known to have been frozen to $74 million, including around $24 million already detailed by the finance ministry in July, some of which had been stolen in the breakaway republic of Chechnya.
Owners of previously frozen MinFins have not received coupon payments.
